Thanks Marissa — a few technical notes to add for Jamal: 

Model recommendations (rapid shortlist)- RW-13B-quant (balanced accuracy / cost) — good for structured output and tool-calling correctness.
- RW-7B-int8 (low-latency fallback) — route low-context queries here for cost savings.

Tool-calling / JSON compliance suggestions- Schema validation: run a strict JSON Schema validation on the model output first; flag any schema failures for one retry with a different decoding/temperature setting before applying fallback logic.
- Retries: implement 1 automatic retry (same model, adjusted temperature/beam) for transient parse errors; if still failing, route to a higher-accuracy model (RW-13B) and log both outputs for regression analysis.
- Deterministic function-calls: for cases where exact field values matter (e.g., ticket_id), we recommend constrained generation (forced fields or structured-answer templates) to reduce ambiguity.

Benchmarks and telemetry we’ll collect during the 48h run:- JSON schema pass rate, per-field precision/recall- Latency p50/p95 per route- Retry frequency and success rate after retry- Cost per 1k requests by route

Jamal — if you can share the dataset URL/drive access and an API key to hit a test fallback route, I’ll wire up the initial run.

-Rishi

Hi Jamal — quick responses on the nested arrays and retries: 

Nested arrays- Our structured-output eval harness supports JSON Schema validation including nested arrays and will compute per-field and per-path accuracy. For arrays we recommend: (a) explicit array length expectations in schema where possible, or (b) include sentinel tokens in prompts to delimit array boundaries.

Retries and latency trade-offs- One automated retry with adjusted decoding parameters (lower temperature + constrained tokens) typically resolves ~60-75% of transient parse errors in our experiments. That single retry adds a median 120-150ms overhead on the failing requests since the retry path is invoked only on parse failure.
- If failure rate is ~3%, expected p95 impact is small (typically <2–3% increase) provided retries are rare. 

Operational controls- We’ll output both the raw model text and the normalized JSON after parsing so you can run offline QA and regression tests. We also recommend storing the pre- and post-retry outputs and a boolean schema_pass flag for downstream auditing.

I’ll set up the eval job once we have Drive access + the test token. Marissa — if you want, I can include a small sample notebook in the Drive folder showing how we perform the schema checks and retries.

-Aditya
